scope: Original Skirmish mockups refinement; no native UI/gameplay edits

prompts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Edit image 1, the original Skirmish six-mission scrolling-map concept. Image 2 is the ACTUAL Campaign Unity screen and is the style reference for the existing Oxanium-like military typography, navy/steel panels, consistent Back and colorful blue/green footer commands. Produce one refined, polished landscape full-screen game UI mockup, same 20:9-ish composition and same large mobile-readable controls as image 1.
PRESERVE the entire approved map-first flow and frame: top-left BACK, SKIRMISH / DESERT BASE header, settings/credits, four large fixed objective tabs left, six large mission cards ON THE MAP in a two-column by three-row grid, selected mission preview and controls right, MAPS blue footer and START BATTLE green footer. No small list and no extra cards. Do not redesign the interface or move missions off the map.
Refinements:
1) Give each card a clear readable unique mission name, smaller catalog ID and one short profile line. Six cards EXACTLY: S001 OUTPOST STRIKE (Ground · Field), S002 COMMAND SIEGE (Ground · Base, selected), S003 AIR RAID (Air · Field), S004 AIRBASE STRIKE (Air · Base), S005 COMBINED ADVANCE (Coming soon), S006 COMBINED SIEGE (Coming soon). The two coming-soon cards retain readable titles with a small lock and subdued art. Names are proposed design copy.
2) Every thumbnail must be clearly distinct but belong to the SAME existing desert town/base setting: ground platoon approaching desert compound; command HQ courtyard with flag; aircraft above town; aircraft over base watchtowers; mixed convoy in outskirts; tanks/aircraft near compound. Reuse the reference world's visual style; no invented playable map or new gameplay. Match the S002 detail preview to its exact card scene.
3) Replace three-star scoring with exactly FOUR small circular difficulty medal badges on every AVAILABLE card, bronze/silver/gold/red, filled for earned and hollow for unearned. Show small caption 'DIFFICULTY MEDALS' once above the grid to clarify. S001 first two earned; S002 bronze earned only; S003 none earned; S004 first three earned. Show no medals for unreleased S005/S006. Avoid an unexplained second selection ring; selected card uses cyan border and title only.
4) Calmer more visible map: retain actual aerial terrain texture; reduce region overlay opacity to around 10–15%, thin cyan boundary only for current region, subdued steel borders for other map zones, NO decorative yellow outlines. Maintain the map's large connected Operations-like regions.
5) Sticky heading above cards reads 'BASE ASSAULT · REGION 1 OF 4', smaller summary '4 AVAILABLE · 2 COMING SOON · 3 COMPLETED' (demo progress). Objective tab BASE ASSAULT shows '3/4 COMPLETE · 2 COMING SOON'; other tabs show simple demo progress counts. Put each selected objective name prominently, never shrink text. Lower edge clearly peeks the next region 'NEXT: FRONTLINE CONTROL' with downward chevron; visible vertical scrollbar. Do not squeeze the six cards.
6) Right pane title 'COMMAND SIEGE', smaller 'S002 · BASE ASSAULT'; image; concise purpose 'Destroy the enemy HQ. Keep yours standing.' Then compact labelled ARMY SIZE row with Standard / War / Large War, Standard selected. Four difficulty buttons in 2×2 grid labelled RECRUIT, REGULAR, VETERAN, COMMANDER with corresponding bronze/silver/gold/red medal icons. REGULAR visibly selected with cyan border AND checkmark. All fit comfortably above footer. Same button backgrounds/borders/sizes as Campaign style reference.
Palette: dark navy, steel borders, white text, restrained cyan selection, colorful green/blue command buttons. No gold panel strokes, no gradient text, no extra player controls, no developer notes, no watermark. This is a menu mockup only. Render all requested text accurately, crisp and readable.

Use case: ui-mockup. Edit Image 1, the original Skirmish map-selection mockup. Image 2 is the actual Campaign UI typography/control style reference; Image 3 is the newly refined Skirmish mission screen to match. Produce one polished wide landscape map-selector UI with the same layout, proportions and mobile-readable type as Image 1.
Preserve top-left BACK, SKIRMISH / CHOOSE MAP, settings and credits. Left rail has five LARGE map rows. Center is one connected aerial atlas with five adjacent navigation zones, readable large map plaques and actual visible terrain. Right is selected map detail with large matching desert-base preview and four objective-family progress rows. Blue QUICK BATTLE footer, green CHOOSE MISSIONS footer. This is step 1; do NOT add individual missions on this screen.
Make the atlas much calmer: mostly natural sandy terrain visible, only 8–12 percent opacity on muted region fills, thin steel boundaries; cyan border and small cyan accent only on SELECTED DESERT BASE. No bright green/red/yellow territories, no heavy outlines, no yellow panel strokes. Keep Operations-like connected zones, and add small corresponding existing-world landmarks: base/city/desert pass/refinery/airfield. Navigation artwork only; not new playable geometry.
The five left rows with thumbnail and map icon are:
DESERT BASE; '4/11 COMPLETE'; '13 COMING SOON' (cyan selected).
CITY CROSSROADS; '0/8 COMPLETE'; '16 COMING SOON'.
MOUNTAIN PASS; '0/6 COMPLETE'; '18 COMING SOON'.
INDUSTRIAL BASIN; '0/4 COMPLETE'; '20 COMING SOON'.
AIRFIELD PLAINS; '24 COMING SOON' (subdued but readable).
All are illustrative design progress; do not add debug/demo labels on the screen itself.
Center plaques show only map names, short bold readable labels; use compact distinct map icons. Do not squeeze progress text into map plaques.
Right panel selected title DESERT BASE. Under it show '11 AVAILABLE · 13 COMING SOON', plus small '24 MISSION SLOTS' to distinguish planned capacity from playable content. Large beautiful matching desert HQ/base image. Then the heading 'OBJECTIVE PROGRESS', followed by four uniform rows with existing game's distinct star/flag/burst/truck objective icons:
BASE ASSAULT — 3/4 COMPLETE — 2 SOON
FRONTLINE CONTROL — 1/3 COMPLETE — 3 SOON
BREAKTHROUGH — 0/2 COMPLETE — 4 SOON
CONVOY ESCORT — 0/2 COMPLETE — 4 SOON
The denominator is available missions, and each family still totals six slots; all counts must match exactly. Include a short purpose 'Choose a map, then select a mission.' and a discreet overall capacity label '5 MAPS · 120 PLANNED SLOTS'. This avoids claiming all120 are released.
Match the actual Campaign reference's typography, navy/steel panel backgrounds, thin borders, standard Back arrow, blue secondary and green primary button sizes. White body text, cyan selected title, all large enough for mobile. Preserve ample space, consistent alignment, no small mission drawer, no tiny captions, no extra navigation, no watermark. Keep map-first / mission-second flow exactly.

Use case: ui-mockup. Make a precise polish edit of Image 1 (Skirmish mission-selection mockup). Image 2 is the newly revised map selector; match its calm, mostly natural terrain and restrained selection overlay. Preserve Image 1's layout, all six large mission cards on the map, distinct thumbnails, proposed mission titles, 4 difficulty medal slots per available card, right detail and army-size/difficulty controls, standard BACK/MAPS/START BATTLE commands, fonts and large mobile spacing.
Change ONLY these items:
1) Greatly soften the blue map tint beneath the mission cards: same natural sandy town texture clearly visible as Image 2, with a pale cyan 8–12% transparent wash. Keep only a thin cyan region boundary (no thick electric outline, no gold/yellow strokes, no saturated blue flood). Keep the 'NEXT: FRONTLINE CONTROL' peeking region and scrollbar.
2) Fix the left rail progress text exactly: BASE ASSAULT '3/4 COMPLETE' and '2 COMING SOON'; FRONTLINE CONTROL '1/3 COMPLETE' and '3 COMING SOON'; BREAKTHROUGH '0/2 COMPLETE' and '4 COMING SOON'; CONVOY ESCORT '0/2 COMPLETE' and '4 COMING SOON'. These counts equal exactly six slots in each family. Existing current heading '4 AVAILABLE · 2 COMING SOON · 3 COMPLETED' is correct and must stay.
3) S005 COMBINED ADVANCE profile is 'Combined · Field'; S006 COMBINED SIEGE profile is 'Combined · Base'. Both retain locks and COMING SOON; no medal row.
4) Use a small green completion check consistently on S001, S002 and S004 because all three have earned at least one difficulty medal. S003 has no completion check and four hollow medal slots. Selected S002 still uses its cyan card border and cyan title. Keep medal counts: S001 bronze/silver earned; S002 bronze only; S003 none; S004 bronze/silver/gold earned. Four slots, never three-star scoring.
5) Let the current-region heading look anchored to the top of the map viewport and make the bottom next-region cue clearly part of the scrolling map. No extra cards, no small mission drawer, no layout change, no new gameplay or new physical maps.
All other image content stays unchanged. The right selected COMMAND SIEGE / S002 preview must remain an exact visual match for S002's thumbnail, purpose 'Destroy the enemy HQ. Keep yours standing.', Standard army size selected, Regular difficulty selected with a check. High-quality crisp landscape game UI, no watermark, no debug labels.
